# Temple Scroll Column 26 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 26 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**26:1** You shall construct gates for the inner court: a gate on the east, a gate on the south, a gate on the north, and a gate on the west.

**26:2** The width of the gates shall be fourteen cubits, corresponding to the width of the foundation wall.

**26:3** Each gate shall have two doors that turn upon their pivots.

**26:4** The height of the gates shall be twenty-eight cubits, from threshold to lintel.

**26:5** You shall overlay the gates with gold, fashioning coverings of refined gold over cedar for the gates.

**26:6** The thresholds of the gates shall each be of a single great stone, their width matching the width of the wall.

**26:7** On each side of every gate you shall erect pillars of cedar overlaid with gold.

**26:8** Each gate shall have a portico, fourteen cubits wide and [...] cubits deep.

**26:9** Above each gate you shall construct a chamber for the gatekeeper who stands watch over the gate.

**26:10** The chambers for the priests and the Levites shall be situated in the colonnades flanking each gate.

**26:11** The chambers south of the eastern gate shall be assigned to the priests who maintain the service of the altar and the house.

**26:12** The chambers north of the eastern gate shall be assigned to the priests who maintain the service of the house and who set the showbread in order.

**26:13** The chambers adjacent to the southern gate shall be assigned to the priests who oversee the sacrifices and examine the offerings for defects.

**26:14** The chambers adjacent to the northern gate shall be assigned to the Levites who minister in the inner court alongside the priests.

**26:15** The gatekeepers — drawn from the sons of Levi — shall guard each gate day and night; they shall not abandon their post.

**26:16** No ritually impure person shall enter through the gates of the inner court. Whoever enters must be clean in body and in garment, for the court is most holy before Me.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 26 well preserved. Four gates at cardinal points with identical proportions (14 cubits wide, 28 cubits high — a 1:2 ratio). The assignment of priestly chambers by gate location reflects an organized hierarchy of temple duties. Lacuna in v.8 for porch depth.*
